title: Geo-priority routing with standby activation safeguards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a geo-priority based routing controller that drives warm-standby activation using conservative safeguards. The goal is to ensure predictable failover across regions and customer tiers while avoiding unnecessary capacity spin-up and cache churn. This ticket covers controller design, readiness metrics, probe choreography, activation throttles, and the rollout plan for Canary + incremental region enablement.
updates: 2025-11-04: Kickoff - scoped to controller, probe spec, and readiness metric set. Stakeholders: Runtime (Marcus, Priya), Platform (Jamal), SRE (Elena).

2025-11-06: Design sync - decided to prefer active readiness probes over solely passive signal to reduce MTTR in noisy telemetry. Trade-off: additional probe traffic vs faster and deterministic activation. Agreed to use a throttled probe cadence and allow probe sampling per customer-tier.

2025-11-07: Readiness metrics defined: 'serve_latency_95_warm', 'kv_cache_hit_ratio_warm', and 'startup_gpu_warm_seconds'. Thresholds drafted in Confluence doc. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Geo+Priority+Standby+Design
2025-11-09: Implementation started - added new controller module 'geo_priority_controller' in runtime repo. First PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1846

2025-11-10: Reviewed probe backoff algorithm with SRE; added hysteresis window of 120s to avoid flapping during transient network issues. Decision logged: staggered KV priming will run at low priority with rate limit to avoid noisy cache churn.

2025-11-11: Integration tests added to CI that simulate regional outage and validate standby activation sequence and rollback on false-positive probes. Initial test run shows 9% extra GPU spin-ups in stress scenario - tuning in progress.

2025-11-12: Design review with PM and Console team. Action items: expose activation state in Console, add dashboard for serve_latency_95_warm and probe success rate, and add a per-tenant activation budget to limit cost spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can select target region based on geo-priority and tier policy and emit activation intent events.
Warm-standby health probe pattern reliably distinguishes 'cold' vs 'ready' states with <5% false-positive activation in synthetic outage tests.
KV priming and prefix cache seeding performed under rate limits to keep incremental token-cost within configured activation budget.
Console surface shows activation state, probe success rate, and predicted activation cost for a given failover event.
Automated integration test simulates regional failure and validates rollback path (controller deactivates standby when primary recovers) within defined SLOs.
timeline: Week 1: finalize probe spec, implement controller scaffolding, and instrumentation points
Week 2: implement activation throttles, KV priming, and add metrics; open PRs
Week 3: run synthetic regional-failure tests, tune thresholds, and add Console hooks
Week 4: Canary release to non-critical regions and monitor cost/activation metrics for two weeks
